source.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the crowds he went up into the mountain; and having sat down of him came to him the disciples of him;

en.L: And seeing the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on the mountain, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sat down, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
en.B: Seeing the crowds, Jesus went up onto the mountain. He sat down, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus saw the crowds of people, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on a hill and sat down. His followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Et voyant les foules, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta sur la montagne, et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se fut assis, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}},
fr.B: Voyant les foules, Jésus monta sur la montagne. Il s’assit, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples vinrent auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus a vu les foules, alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est monté sur une colline et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est assis. Ses disciples sont venus près de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

decisions.choice: went up on the mountain: perhaps an echo of Moses on Sinai
alternatives: only a place where the crowd could hear
decisions.reason: Moses went up the mountain to receive the law (Exodus 19:3). Here Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches what the law means (5:17-48). Matthew does not name the mountain or draw the comparison.

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers sat to teach (23:2; Luke 4:20).

decisions.choice: his disciples, with the crowds also listening
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to his disciples, but at the end the crowds are amazed at his teaching (7:28-29).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what disciples are.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); the sermon itself is speech and keeps the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 1-4 and the other Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken. What Jesus says in the sermon is in the tenses of speech ("on a persécuté les prophètes", 5:12).

decisions.choice: ses disciples at Readable too
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers". The term sheet keeps "les disciples" at every level, as Mark and Luke do; French "disciple" is a common word for someone who learns from a master.

source.text: καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·

records.literal_gloss: And having opened the mouth of him he was teaching them saying:

en.L: and opening {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them, saying:
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them. He said:

fr.L: et ouvrant {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseignait, disant :
fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à les enseigner :
fr.R: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a commencé à les enseigner. Il disait :

decisions.choice: opening his mouth: a solemn way to begin an important speech
decisions.reason: The phrase marks what follows as weighty teaching (compare Job 3:1; Acts 8:35).

decisions.choice: began to teach them
alternatives: opened his mouth and taught them
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures the teaching under way. Balanced and Readable say he began, and leave out the idiom, which the meaning note explains.

source.text: Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the poor in the spirit, for of them is the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: "Blessed [are] the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
en.B: "Blessed are those who are poor in spirit: the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
en.R: "Blessed are those who know they are poor and need God. The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.

fr.L: « Heureux les pauvres en esprit, car à eux est le royaume des cieux.
fr.B: « Heureux ceux qui sont pauvres en esprit : le royaume des cieux leur appartient.
fr.R: « Ils sont heureux, ceux qui savent qu’ils sont pauvres et qu’ils ont besoin de Dieu. Le royaume des cieux est à eux.

decisions.choice: blessed: in the happy state of those God favors
alternatives: may they be blessed, as a wish
decisions.reason: The word describes people who are well off in God's eyes, whatever they feel. Each saying states a fact about them and gives the reason in what God will do. The form is known from the Psalms and Proverbs (Psalm 1:1; 32:1).

decisions.choice: poor in spirit: those who know they have nothing to offer God and depend on him
decisions.reason: In the Psalms and Isaiah the poor are the humble who look to God for help (Psalm 34:7, 19; Isaiah 61:1; 66:2). "In spirit" makes clear that an inner poverty is meant, though Jesus's hearers included many who were poor in fact.

decisions.choice: theirs is the kingdom: the first and last sayings promise the kingdom now
decisions.reason: The first saying and the eighth (5:10) both have "is"; the six between have "will". The kingdom frames the list, and its blessings are both present and to come.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: those who know they are poor and need God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase.

decisions.choice: Heureux (L, B); Ils sont heureux, ceux qui ... (R), for all the beatitudes (5:3-11)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 6:20: "heureux" is the usual French word for the beatitudes and says the happy state of those God favours (m1); "bienheureux" now sounds churchly or suggests the blessed in heaven, and "béni" belongs to another Greek word. Readable turns the exclamation, which has no verb, into a plain sentence; Luke's Readable says "Vous êtes heureux" because Luke's sayings are in the second person.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the mourning, for they will be comforted.

en.L: Blessed [are] those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
en.B: Blessed are those who mourn: they will be comforted.
en.R: Blessed are those who are sad and grieving. God will comfort them.

fr.L: Heureux ceux qui pleurent, car ils seront consolés.
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui sont en deuil : ils recevront la consolation.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux qui sont tristes et en deuil. Dieu les consolera.

decisions.choice: those who mourn ... will be comforted: an echo of Isaiah 61:2
alternatives: grief of any kind with no echo
decisions.reason: Isaiah 61:1-3 promises good news to the poor and comfort to all who mourn, the mourners of Zion. Jesus's words recall that promise; the mourning includes grief over sin and over the state of God's people.

decisions.choice: will be comforted: God is the one who will do it
decisions.reason: Jewish speech often used the passive to speak of what God does without naming him. Readable names God.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: God will comfort them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

en.L: Blessed [are] the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
en.B: Blessed are the gentle: they will inherit the earth.
en.R: Blessed are those who are gentle and humble. God will give them the earth as their own.

fr.L: Heureux les doux, car ils hériteront la terre.
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui sont doux : la terre leur sera donnée en héritage.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux qui sont doux et humbles. Dieu leur donnera la terre pour qu’elle soit à eux.

decisions.choice: the meek will inherit the earth: Psalm 37:11
decisions.reason: Psalm 37:11 says that the meek will inherit the land. There the land is Israel's promised land; Jesus widens it to the whole earth renewed (19:28).

decisions.choice: meek: gentle and humble, not grasping or violent
decisions.reason: The word describes those who do not push for their own way and leave their cause with God. Jesus uses it of himself (11:29; 21:5).

decisions.choice: the earth
decisions.reason: The same word means land or earth. In the psalm it is the land; here, in a saying addressed to all disciples, the wider sense fits.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: gentle (B); gentle and humble (R)
decisions.reason: "Meek" can now suggest weakness. Balanced and Readable use words for the quality meant.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the hungering and thirsting [for] the righteousness, for they will be filled.

en.L: Blessed [are] those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
en.B: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness: they will be satisfied.
en.R: Blessed are those who long for righteousness the way a hungry person longs for food and a thirsty person for water. God will give them all they long for.

fr.L: Heureux ceux qui ont faim et qui ont soif de la justice, car eux seront rassasiés.
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui ont faim et soif de justice : ils seront comblés.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux qui désirent la justice autant qu’une personne affamée désire manger et qu’une personne assoiffée désire boire. Dieu leur donnera tout ce qu’ils désirent.

decisions.choice: righteousness: right living before God, and God setting things right
decisions.reason: In Matthew righteousness is doing God's will (5:10, 20; 6:1, 33). Those who long for it want to live rightly and want God's justice in the world. Both are in view.

decisions.choice: will be filled: God is the one who will do it
decisions.reason: Jewish speech often used the passive to speak of what God does without naming him. Readable names God.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: the way a hungry person longs for food; God will give them all they long for
alternatives: hunger and thirst for; will be filled
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture and names God.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

en.L: Blessed [are] the merciful, for they will receive mercy.
en.B: Blessed are the merciful: mercy will be shown to them.
en.R: Blessed are those who show mercy to others. God will show mercy to them.

fr.L: Heureux les miséricordieux, car ils recevront miséricorde.
fr.B: Heureux les miséricordieux : il leur sera fait miséricorde.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux qui ont pitié des autres. Dieu aura pitié d’eux.

decisions.choice: the merciful will receive mercy: from God, at the judgment
decisions.reason: Matthew links mercy given and mercy received (6:12, 14-15; 18:33). The passive points to God.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: God will show mercy to them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the pure in the heart, for they the God will see.

en.L: Blessed [are] the pure in heart, for they will see God.
en.B: Blessed are the pure in heart: they will see God.
en.R: Blessed are those whose hearts are pure. They will see God.

fr.L: Heureux les purs de cœur, car ils verront Dieu.
fr.B: Heureux les cœurs purs : ils verront Dieu.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux dont le cœur est pur. Ils verront Dieu.

decisions.choice: pure in heart: undivided in devotion to God (Psalm 24:3-4)
decisions.reason: Psalm 24 asks who may stand in God's presence and answers: those with clean hands and a pure heart. The heart is the whole inner person.

decisions.choice: will see God: be in his presence
decisions.reason: Seeing God is the hope of being with him (Psalm 17:15; Revelation 22:4).

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the peacemakers, for they sons of God will be called.

en.L: Blessed [are] the peacemakers, for they will be called {{gender:children|sons}} of God.
en.B: Blessed are those who make peace: they will be called {{gender:children|sons}} of God.
en.R: Blessed are those who work to bring peace. God will call them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:children|sons}}.

fr.L: Heureux les artisans de paix, car ils seront appelés {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu.
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui font la paix : ils seront appelés {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux qui travaillent à faire la paix. Dieu les appellera {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} {{gender:enfants|fils}}.

decisions.choice: peacemakers: those who make peace between people
decisions.reason: The word is active: people who bring about peace where there is quarrel and hatred (5:23-24, 44).

decisions.choice: called sons of God: God will own them as his children
decisions.reason: "Son of" describes likeness and belonging; those who make peace are like the God of peace (5:45). The word includes all of them, men and women.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive default says who is meant; the traditional form keeps "sons".

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the having been persecuted on account of righteousness, for of them is the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: Blessed [are] those who have been persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
en.B: Blessed are those who suffer persecution for the sake of righteousness: the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
en.R: Blessed are those who are treated badly because they do what is righteous. The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.

fr.L: Heureux ceux qui ont été persécutés à cause de la justice, car à eux est le royaume des cieux.
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui sont persécutés pour la cause de la justice : le royaume des cieux leur appartient.
fr.R: Ils sont heureux, ceux qu’on maltraite parce qu’ils font ce qui est juste. Le royaume des cieux est à eux.

decisions.choice: for the sake of righteousness: because they do what God requires
decisions.reason: They suffer for living rightly, as in 5:6. The next saying makes the cause Jesus himself (5:11).

decisions.choice: theirs is the kingdom: the same promise as the first saying
decisions.reason: The repetition closes the eight sayings (see 5:3).

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

source.text: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθ’ ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed are you when they insult you and persecute and say every evil against you lying on account of me.

en.L: Blessed are you when they insult you and persecute [you] and say every evil [thing] against you, lying, because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: You are blessed when people abuse you and persecute you and spread all sorts of evil lies about you for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake.
en.R: You are blessed when people say bad things about you and hurt you and tell lies about you because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Heureux êtes-vous quand on vous insultera, et [vous] persécutera, et dira contre vous toute sorte de mal en mentant, à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Vous êtes heureux quand on vous insulte, qu’on vous persécute et qu’on répand sur vous toutes sortes de mensonges malveillants à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Vous êtes heureux quand les gens disent du mal de vous, quand ils vous font souffrir et racontent des mensonges sur vous parce que vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivez.

decisions.choice: blessed are you: Jesus now speaks to his hearers directly
alternatives: a ninth blessing like the others
decisions.reason: The sayings change from "those who" to "you", and the cause becomes loyalty to Jesus.

decisions.choice: lying: what they say about you is false
decisions.reason: The word limits the blessing: it is for those who are slandered falsely.

decisions.choice: because you follow me
decisions.reason: Readable says why they are treated this way.

source.text: χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Rejoice and be glad, for the reward of you [is] great in the heavens; thus for they persecuted the prophets the before you.

en.L: Rejoice and be glad, for your reward [is] great in the heavens, for in this way they persecuted the prophets who [were] before you.
en.B: Rejoice and celebrate, because a great reward is waiting for you in heaven. That is how they persecuted the prophets who came before you.
en.R: Be happy and celebrate! You will have a great reward in heaven. People treated the prophets who lived before you in the same way.

fr.L: Réjouissez-vous et exultez, car votre récompense [est] grande dans les cieux ; car ainsi ils ont persécuté les prophètes qui [étaient] avant vous.
fr.B: Réjouissez-vous, débordez de joie, car une grande récompense vous attend dans le ciel. Les prophètes venus avant vous ont été persécutés de la même façon.
fr.R: Soyez contents et faites la fête ! Vous aurez une grande récompense dans le ciel. Les gens ont traité de la même façon les prophètes qui ont vécu avant vous.

decisions.choice: your reward in heaven: what God has kept for you
decisions.reason: Heaven here is where God keeps what he will give (6:20). The reward is his gift, not wages.

decisions.choice: the prophets before you: those whom Israel rejected and persecuted
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was beaten and imprisoned (Jeremiah 20:2; 37:15); Jesus later speaks of the killing of prophets (23:29-37). The disciples stand in their line.

source.text: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται;

records.literal_gloss: You are the salt of the earth; if but the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be salted?

en.L: You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be made salty?
en.B: You are the salt for the earth. But if salt goes flat, what can give it back its saltiness?
en.R: You are like salt for all the people on earth. But if salt loses its taste, there is no way to make it salty again.

fr.L: Vous êtes le sel de la terre ; mais si le sel devient fade, avec quoi sera-t-il salé ?
fr.B: Vous êtes le sel pour la terre. Mais si le sel perd sa saveur, qu’est-ce qui pourra lui rendre son goût salé ?
fr.R: Vous êtes comme du sel pour tous les gens de la terre. Mais si le sel perd son goût, il n’y a aucun moyen de le rendre salé à nouveau.

decisions.choice: salt: what gives flavor and keeps food from spoiling
decisions.reason: Salt seasoned food and preserved it. The disciples are what the world needs in order to be what God wants.

decisions.choice: becomes tasteless: loses its saltiness
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "be foolish" or "become tasteless". Salt from the Dead Sea was mixed with other minerals, and the salt could leach out, leaving something that looked like salt but had no taste.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: with what will it be salted?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "nothing". Readable gives the answer.

source.text: εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: For nothing it is strong any longer except having been thrown out to be trampled by the men.

en.L: It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: It is good for nothing anymore but to be thrown out and walked on.
en.R: It is not good for anything. It gets thrown out, and people walk on it.

fr.L: Il n’est plus bon à rien, sinon à être jeté dehors et piétiné par les {{gender:gens|hommes}}.
fr.B: Il n’est plus bon à rien qu’à être jeté dehors et piétiné.
fr.R: Il n’est plus bon à rien. On le jette dehors, et les gens marchent dessus.

decisions.choice: thrown out and trampled: a warning of judgment
decisions.reason: Being thrown out is a picture of rejection at the judgment (8:12; 13:48). Disciples who lose what makes them disciples are useless.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:gens|hommes}} for the plural of the word for human beings, in this sermon (5:13, 5:16)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 6:22: the word means people in general, and "les gens" is the natural inclusive French for that; "les humains" would sound as if humanity were set against something else. The traditional "les hommes" is the alternative.

source.text: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: You are the light of the world.

en.L: You are the light of the world.
en.B: You are the light of the world.
en.R: You are like a light for the whole world.

fr.L: Vous êtes la lumière du monde.
fr.B: Vous êtes la lumière du monde.
fr.R: Vous êtes comme une lumière pour le monde entier.

decisions.choice: the light of the world: Israel's calling to be a light to the nations
decisions.reason: God called his servant to be "a light for the nations" (Isaiah 42:6; 49:6). Jesus gives that calling to his disciples. In 4:16 Jesus himself is the light.

source.text: οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·

records.literal_gloss: Not is able a city to be hidden on a hill lying;

en.L: A city lying on a hill cannot be hidden.
en.B: A town built on a hilltop cannot be hidden.
en.R: Everyone can see a town that is built on top of a hill.

fr.L: Une ville située sur une colline ne peut pas être cachée.
fr.B: On ne peut cacher une ville bâtie au sommet d’une colline.
fr.R: Tout le monde peut voir une ville construite en haut d’une colline.

decisions.choice: a city on a hill: seen from far away
decisions.reason: Towns were often built on hills and their white walls could be seen for miles. Some hear an echo of Jerusalem on Mount Zion (Isaiah 2:2-3).

decisions.choice: everyone can see
decisions.reason: Readable says it positively.

source.text: οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Nor do they light a lamp and put it under the basket, but on the lampstand, and it shines to all the in the house.

en.L: Nor do they light a lamp and put it under the basket, but on the lampstand, and it shines for all who [are] in the house.
en.B: No one lights a lamp and hides it under a basket; it goes on a lampstand, where it shines for everyone in the house.
en.R: People do not light a lamp and then cover it with a bowl. They put it up high on a stand, so it gives light to everyone in the house.

fr.L: Et on n’allume pas non plus une lampe pour la mettre sous le boisseau, mais sur le porte-lampe, et elle brille pour tous ceux qui [sont] dans la maison.
fr.B: Personne n’allume une lampe pour la cacher sous un récipient ; on la pose sur son support, et elle éclaire tous ceux qui sont dans la maison.
fr.R: Les gens n’allument pas une lampe pour la couvrir ensuite avec un seau. Ils la posent en hauteur sur un support, et elle éclaire tout le monde dans la maison.

decisions.choice: a lamp under the basket: a small clay oil lamp and a grain measure
decisions.reason: Houses had one room and a small oil lamp. The basket was a measure for grain that held about two gallons; put over the lamp, it would hide the light or put it out.

decisions.choice: No one (B); People (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "they" means people in general.

decisions.choice: a bowl
decisions.reason: Readable names a common container.

decisions.choice: le boisseau (L); un récipient (B); un seau (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 4:21: the Greek names a grain measure (m1), which French has long called "boisseau", and "mettre sous le boisseau" is still a French idiom for hiding something; Literal keeps it. Balanced and Readable use a common container, the same words as Mark.

source.text: οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Thus let shine the light of you before the men, so that they may see of you the good works and may glorify the Father of you the in the heavens.

en.L: In the same way let your light shine before {{gender:people|men}}, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who [is] in the heavens.
en.B: In the same way, your light must shine where people can see it, so that they will see your good deeds and give glory to your Father in heaven.
en.R: In the same way, let your light shine for people to see. Then they will see the good things you do, and they will give glory to your Father in heaven.

fr.L: De même, que votre lumière brille devant les {{gender:gens|hommes}}, afin qu’ils voient vos bonnes œuvres et qu’ils glorifient votre Père qui [est] dans les cieux.
fr.B: De la même manière, votre lumière doit briller là où les gens peuvent la voir, afin qu’ils voient le bien que vous faites et rendent gloire à votre Père qui est dans le ciel.
fr.R: De la même façon, faites briller votre lumière pour que les gens la voient. Alors ils verront le bien que vous faites, et ils rendront gloire à votre Père qui est dans le ciel.

decisions.choice: so that they glorify your Father: the good deeds point people to God
alternatives: so that the disciples are praised
decisions.reason: The aim is God's honor, not the disciples' (6:1). The Father in heaven is a name for God that Matthew uses often.

decisions.choice: good works: deeds of mercy and obedience that others can see
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the whole of a life lived as 5:3-12 describes.

decisions.choice: give glory to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the noun form, which keeps the key term.
